## The Core Challenge: People, Not Technology

The biggest blocker to AI success is not the technology—it's the operating model of the humans trying to use it. While technology accelerates, people's readiness often falls behind.

AI transformation fails when leaders treat it as automation, efficiency, or a technology rollout. It succeeds when they treat it as a capability change, a mindset shift, a workflow redesign, and ultimately, a business model evolution.

## Key Human Barriers to Adoption

Human factors remain the biggest barrier to successful adoption, with more than half of organizations citing challenges like resistance to change, lack of clarity, and skill gaps.

While employees are broadly enthusiastic about working with AI, that optimism is often undermined by job insecurity, skills anxiety and unclear direction from leadership. A 2025 Pew Research survey found that 52% of U.S. workers are worried about AI's long-term impact on their careers, and another poll showed that 71% of Americans fear AI will lead to permanent job reductions.

## The Mental and Emotional Toll

A 2025 Nature study found that AI adoption was associated with higher employee depression, with job insecurity and emotional exhaustion helping explain the relationship, and Harvard Business Review has warned of "AI brain fry," the mental fatigue that can come from excessive use or oversight of AI tools.

## Critical Success Factors

When employees understand how work will change through AI and that human judgment still matters, AI adoption will increase while AI anxiety will decrease.

"Change fitness" is the capacity to metabolize significant and ongoing change. At the individual level, it shows up as curiosity, experimentation, and comfort working in human–machine workflows. At the team level, it means new collaboration patterns, role clarity, and decision rights that match an AI-driven context. At the organizational level, it requires modern data foundations, thoughtful governance, and leaders who treat AI as a transformation of work, not just a software rollout.

The companies seeing real returns from AI are those that treat people as the catalyst, not the constraint.

# WalkMe Homepage: Taglines, Headlines & Positioning

## Hero Headlines & Taglines
- **"WalkMe turns AI potential into AI performance."**
- **"WalkMe is the critical layer that makes enterprise AI work."**
- **"This is what AI was supposed to feel like."**
- **"Trusted by the companies that run the world."**

## AI-Focused Positioning
- **"Omnipresent contextual AI assistance"** (WalkMe AI tagline)
- **"The gap between your AI investment and your AI results is smaller than you think."**

## ROI & Adoption Claims
- **"30% fewer support tickets"**
- **"1.5M hours of productivity returned"**
- **"150%+ more self-service completions"**
- **"WalkMe delivers a 3-year 494% ROI"** (IDC study)

## Target Audience
The platform addresses **four primary personas**:
1. **Sales teams** – deal protection, approval workflows
2. **HR departments** – onboarding, compliance training, enrollment
3. **IT/Management** – AI ROI measurement, adoption analytics
4. **Customer Care agents** – ticket resolution, first-contact completion

Secondary audiences include enterprises managing **digital transformation, change management, and regulated industries**.

# The Human Side of AI Adoption: EY's Messaging Analysis

## Primary Headlines & Taglines

**Main positioning:**
- "Why every AI strategy is a people strategy"
- "AI adoption isn't just a technology challenge — it's a human one"

## Key Messaging Pillars

**Emotional/Strategic Angle:**
The core narrative frames AI success as fundamentally dependent on *people*, not technology. EY positions organizations that prioritize transparency, engagement, and skill-building as those achieving real returns—positioning people as "the catalyst, not the constraint."

## Target Audience

**Primary C-suite audiences:**
- **CEOs/COOs**: Strategic leadership and organizational transformation
- **CHROs/Talent Leaders**: Recruitment, L&D, and workforce development
- **Business Leaders**: General adoption and ROI concerns

## Core Story Frame

Four chapters structure the narrative:

1. **Recruitment reimagined** — AI is reshaping hiring practices
2. **Leadership & learning** — Structured upskilling drives adoption
3. **Employee engagement** — Clear communication directly influences success
4. **Where adoption succeeds** — Leadership choices matter more than tools

## Representative Quote

"We have to train our leaders to have different conversations with their people—conversations about value and impact." — Ginnie Carlier, EY Chief Talent and Culture Officer

**Strategic positioning:** AI as a *people transformation* challenge requiring executive commitment to transparency and continuous learning.

# AI Adoption vs. Adaptation: Key Headlines and Insights

## Main Headlines
- **"AI adoption to adaptation: How a new change approach can build the human behaviors needed for AI"**
- **"AI adoption is easy to prove and easy to fake"**

## Critical Statistics on People-Driven Failure

- Worker access to AI tools expanded 50% in one year, yet **fewer than 60% actually use AI daily**
- **84% of organizations haven't redesigned jobs or workflows around AI**
- Only **50% of executives regularly verify AI output quality**
- **69% of workers report increased workload** despite AI implementation
- **43% cite lack of time** as their biggest adaptation barrier
- Only **56% feel recognized for being adaptive**, despite 78% experimenting

## Key Behavioral Quotes

**"Too many organizations treat AI as an adoption problem without first asking how you can achieve the outcomes desired. What's really required is behavioral change."**
— Michael Ehret, Walmart International CPO

**"Adoption tells you someone opened the door. It tells you nothing about whether they changed how they work."**
— Article core argument

**"A key part of judgment is knowing when to use AI and when not to."**
— Margaret Greenleaf, Roche

## Target Audience

Senior HR leaders, organizational transformation executives, and chief human resources officers managing enterprise AI implementation at scale.

# The Human Side of AI Adoption: Key Arguments and Framing

## Core Argument
The article argues that AI adoption lags in conservative industries not because of technological limitations, but because leaders underestimate human resistance. Success requires three strategic approaches: demystifying AI through familiar examples, integrating it into existing workflows, and measuring impact using metrics employees already understand.

## Verbatim Key Quotes (Under 125 Characters)

**On the core problem:**
- "AI adoption fails because leaders underestimate the human and operational context in which AI tools are introduced"
- "front-line skepticism is not resistance to progress — it's just a rational human response"

**On accessibility:**
- "When you can't comprehend something, you start developing a fear of it"

**On change fatigue (not technology aversion):**
- "change fatigue, not an aversion to technology, is the real blocker"

**On the solution approach:**
- "When AI meets people where they already work, curiosity replaces resistance"
- "user comfort and trust, not algorithms, ultimately determine whether AI delivers"

## Story Frame & Emotional Angle
The narrative positions late-adopter industries as rational and cautious rather than backwards. The emotional journey moves from fear and alienation → understanding → acceptance, framing workers' hesitation as legitimate rather than obstinate. Success comes through respect for existing workflows, not disruption.

# The "Human Side of Change" in AI Adoption — Narrative Landscape 2025–2026

Who owns the "AI adoption is a people problem, not a tech problem" story, what exact language they use, and where the white space is.

---

## 1. Who OWNS the "AI adoption = change, not technology" narrative

This frame is now **mainstream and crowded**. Every major consultancy, the change-management establishment, and the DAP vendors have all planted flags on it. The strongest verbatim ownership:

### McKinsey
- **Frame:** Workflow redesign, not the model, drives value. Regression across 25 org attributes found **"end-to-end workflow redesign has the single strongest effect on whether enterprises see bottom-line EBIT impact from generative AI."**
- The **10-20-70 principle** (widely cited, McKinsey-origin): **"70% of AI efforts to people, processes, and cultural transformation; 20% to data and technology infrastructure; only 10% to algorithms and models."** This single statistic is the numeric backbone of the entire "it's the people" narrative.
- Reports: *The State of Organizations 2026*; *State of AI trust in 2026: Shifting to the agentic era*.
- **Audience:** CEO / COO / board.
- URL: https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/tech-and-ai/our-insights/tech-forward/state-of-ai-trust-in-2026-shifting-to-the-agentic-era

### BCG
- **Frame:** "Beyond adoption." Deployment isn't the finish line — redesigning the flow of work is.
- Headline: **"Companies Must Go Beyond AI Adoption to Realize Its Full Potential"** (press, 26 June 2025).
- **Audience:** CEO / CIO.
- URL: https://www.bcg.com/press/26june2025-beyond-ai-adoption-full-potential

### Deloitte
- **Frame:** The sharpest reframe in the whole landscape — **"adoption" vs "adaptation."** Adoption is fake progress; behavioral change is the real thing.
- Verbatim headlines: **"AI adoption to adaptation: How a new change approach can build the human behaviors needed for AI"** and **"AI adoption is easy to prove and easy to fake."**
- Core line: **"Adoption tells you someone opened the door. It tells you nothing about whether they changed how they work."**
- Quote (Michael Ehret, Walmart International CPO): **"Too many organizations treat AI as an adoption problem without first asking how you can achieve the outcomes desired. What's really required is behavioral change."**
- Stats they cite: **84% of organizations haven't redesigned jobs or workflows around AI**; **69% of workers report increased workload** despite AI; fewer than 60% with access use AI daily.
- **Audience:** CHRO / senior HR / transformation execs.
- URL: https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/topics/talent/ai-adoption-to-ai-adaptation.html

### EY
- **Frame:** "Every AI strategy is a people strategy." People as catalyst, not constraint.
- Verbatim: **"Why every AI strategy is a people strategy"** and **"AI adoption isn't just a technology challenge — it's a human one."**
- Quote (Ginnie Carlier, EY Chief Talent and Culture Officer): **"We have to train our leaders to have different conversations with their people — conversations about value and impact."**
- **Audience:** CEO/COO + CHRO/talent leaders.
- URL: https://www.ey.com/en_us/services/entrepreneurship/the-human-side-of-ai-adoption

### MIT Sloan Management Review (Ganes Kesari)
- **Frame:** Front-line skepticism is rational; change fatigue, not tech aversion, is the blocker.
- Verbatim: **"AI adoption fails because leaders underestimate the human and operational context in which AI tools are introduced"**; **"front-line skepticism is not resistance to progress — it's just a rational human response"**; **"change fatigue, not an aversion to technology, is the real blocker"**; **"user comfort and trust, not algorithms, ultimately determine whether AI delivers."**
- **Audience:** senior leaders / practitioners.
- URL: https://sloanreview.mit.edu/article/the-human-side-of-ai-adoption-lessons-from-the-field/

---

## 2. The specific phrases and framing — who owns each

| Phrase | Primary owners | Verbatim usage |
|---|---|---|
| **"The human side of AI adoption"** | EY, MIT SMR, HRO Today | Used near-identically as article/service titles — this exact phrase is heavily saturated. |
| **"People-centric / people-first"** | **Prosci** (owns this), Deloitte | Prosci: *"AI Transformation: A People-Centric Guide to Leading Change"*; *"AI Adoption: Driving Change With a People-First Approach."* |
| **"People side of change"** | **Prosci** (their decades-old trademark territory, now pointed at AI) | Prosci's foundational brand language, re-skinned for AI. |
| **"Change fatigue"** | MIT SMR, Harvard/HBS | HBS 2026: building **"change fitness"** — *"the capacity to metabolize significant and ongoing change."* MIT: change fatigue "is the real blocker." |
| **"Adoption gap"** | WalkMe, Futurum | WalkMe: **"the costly digital adoption gap."** |
| **"The last mile of transformation"** | DAP vendors (implicit); less explicitly claimed — see white space | Framed as "in the flow of work" rather than "last mile." |
| **"Resistance" / "hearts and minds"** | Change-management playbooks, WEF | Digital Applied 2026 playbook: *"Overcoming Resistance."* "Hearts and minds" is surprisingly under-used verbatim — mostly paraphrased as "trust and comfort." |
| **"Catalyst, not the constraint"** | EY / WEF ecosystem | *"treat people as the catalyst, not the constraint."* |

Notable: **"AI brain fry"** (HBR) and **"change fitness"** (HBS) are fresher, less-crowded coinages.

---

## 3. AI-adoption players positioning on the human/behavioral side

### WalkMe (SAP-owned Digital Adoption Platform)
- **What it is:** Overlay layer on top of enterprise apps giving in-context guidance, automation, and adoption analytics.
- **Verbatim taglines:** **"WalkMe turns AI potential into AI performance."** · **"WalkMe is the critical layer that makes enterprise AI work."** · **"This is what AI was supposed to feel like."** · **"The gap between your AI investment and your AI results is smaller than you think."**
- Q2 2026 release theme: **"What If Work Just Knew?"**
- ROI-led proof: *"3-year 494% ROI"* (IDC), *"1.5M hours of productivity returned."*
- **Audience:** CIO / IT + HR + sales ops. Very ROI/CFO-flavored.
- URL: https://www.walkme.com/

### Whatfix (DAP)
- **What it is:** In-app guidance + analytics to drive software/AI adoption "in the flow of work."
- **Verbatim taglines:** **"Software Clicks Better With Whatfix"** · **"Accelerating AI Value in the Flow of Work"** · **"Deploying AI ≠ Using AI"** · **"Low Adoption = Wasted Investment"** · **"Without adoption support, employees fall back on old workflows."**
- Owns the phrase **"User Experience Gap"** for why AI pilots fail; leans on the **"95% of AI pilots don't scale"** stat.
- Stat: *"Employees who are early AI adopters have 40% higher-quality output"* and *"only 1% call their AI strategy 'mature.'"*
- **Audience:** enterprise L&D, HR, app owners, C-suite ROI.
- URLs: https://whatfix.com/solutions/ai-adoption/ · https://whatfix.com/

### Prosci (the change-management incumbent)
- **What it is:** The legacy change-management methodology firm (ADKAR) repositioning onto AI. **The clearest pure-play "people side of change" owner.**
- Language: *"A People-Centric Guide to Leading Change,"* *"Driving Change With a People-First Approach,"* plus a dedicated *"Why AI Transformation Fails"* asset.
- **Audience:** change managers, CHROs, transformation offices.
- URLs: https://www.prosci.com/blog/ai-transformation · https://www.prosci.com/ai-change-management · https://www.prosci.com/blog/why-ai-transformation-fails

### Pendo, Appcues, ClickLearn, Fullstory
- Adjacent DAP/analytics players circling the same "adoption not deployment" story, mostly via WalkMe-alternative comparison content. Less distinct narrative — they ride the category frame rather than own a phrase.

**Note on AI-native change startups:** There is **no dominant AI-native "change/adoption" startup brand** yet. The category is still owned by (a) legacy DAPs (WalkMe/Whatfix) adding AI, and (b) legacy change-management firms (Prosci) adding AI. The "AI-native" label in 2025-2026 sources refers to *product* startups compressing ARR, not to change-management tooling. **This is a white-space signal (see below).**

---

## 4. "AI adoption failure is a people problem" — the stats and emotional angle

The failure-rate narrative is the emotional engine of the whole category. The most-cited numbers:

- **MIT (State of AI in Business 2025): 95% of companies fail to achieve meaningful ROI** — *"the primary barriers being organizational rather than technical."* This is THE headline stat everyone quotes.
- **RAND 2025: 80.3% of enterprise AI projects fail** to deliver business value (33.8% abandoned pre-production).
- **"70% of enterprise AI initiatives fail"** — and *"the failure is not technical. What fails is adoption: the human process of changing how people work, what they trust, and what they do every day."*
- **"63% of AI implementation challenges stem from human factors, not technical limitations."**
- **S&P Global 2025: 42% of companies abandoned most of their AI initiatives** (up from 17% a year earlier); abandonment rate up **147% YoY**.
- **10-20-70:** technology is only ~30% of what drives success.

**Emotional angle** (this is where the human narrative gets its charge):
- **Fear/insecurity:** Pew 2025 — **52% of US workers worried about AI's long-term career impact**; 71% fear permanent job reductions.
- **Mental toll:** a **2025 Nature study linked AI adoption to higher employee depression** (via job insecurity + emotional exhaustion); HBR's **"AI brain fry."**
- **Dignity/respect frame:** MIT SMR reframes skepticism as **rational**, not backward — *"When you can't comprehend something, you start developing a fear of it,"* and *"When AI meets people where they already work, curiosity replaces resistance."*
- **WEF (Jan 2026):** change management + human oversight are **"non-negotiable when leading through AI."**

---

## CROWDED vs WHITE SPACE

**Deeply crowded (avoid competing head-on):**
- "The human side of AI adoption" as a phrase — EY, MIT, HRO Today all use it near-verbatim.
- "It's people not technology / 70-30" — every consultancy owns a version.
- "95% of AI fails / adoption gap" doom-stat — table stakes now.
- Enterprise DAP "in the flow of work" guidance (WalkMe/Whatfix locked this).
- CHRO/CEO-targeted thought leadership from the Big 4.

**White space (openings):**
1. **The individual employee, not the enterprise.** All the incumbents talk *to the C-suite about employees in aggregate.* Almost nobody speaks *to the individual worker* as the customer. NanoClaw's "one agent per employee / the employee grows by managing their agent" is precisely this un-owned angle.
2. **No AI-native change/adoption startup brand exists.** The frame is owned by legacy DAPs bolting on AI and legacy change firms (Prosci) bolting on AI. A genuinely AI-native "bring people across the bridge" brand is unclaimed.
3. **"Hearts and minds" verbatim is under-used** — mostly paraphrased as "trust and comfort." Available.
4. **Emotional/dignity framing at the individual level.** The stats on fear/depression exist, but the incumbents use them as a *problem to manage from above*, not as *empathy toward the person crossing over*. The empathetic, human-to-human "I'll walk you across" voice (Elia's guide/pilot positioning) is nearly empty in this competitive set.
5. **"Adaptation not adoption" (Deloitte)** is a strong reframe but still enterprise/HR-framed — the consumer/individual translation of it is open.

---

**Sources:** [McKinsey State of AI trust 2026](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/tech-and-ai/our-insights/tech-forward/state-of-ai-trust-in-2026-shifting-to-the-agentic-era) · [BCG Beyond AI Adoption](https://www.bcg.com/press/26june2025-beyond-ai-adoption-full-potential) · [Deloitte Adoption to Adaptation](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/topics/talent/ai-adoption-to-ai-adaptation.html) · [EY Human Side of AI Adoption](https://www.ey.com/en_us/services/entrepreneurship/the-human-side-of-ai-adoption) · [MIT SMR Human Side of AI Adoption](https://sloanreview.mit.edu/article/the-human-side-of-ai-adoption-lessons-from-the-field/) · [Prosci AI Transformation](https://www.prosci.com/blog/ai-transformation) · [Prosci AI Change Management](https://www.prosci.com/ai-change-management) · [WalkMe](https://www.walkme.com/) · [Whatfix AI Adoption](https://whatfix.com/solutions/ai-adoption/) · [WEF Change Management Non-Negotiable](https://www.weforum.org/stories/2026/01/why-change-management-and-human-oversight-are-non-negotiable-when-leading-through-ai/) · [HBS Change Fitness 2026](https://www.library.hbs.edu/working-knowledge/ai-trends-for-2026-building-change-fitness-and-balancing-trade-offs) · [RAND/failure stats via Pertama](https://www.pertamapartners.com/insights/ai-project-failure-statistics-2026) · [Change management people-side playbook](https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/change-management-ai-adoption-2026-overcoming-resistance-playbook)

Report is delivered above as structured English markdown. Key takeaway for positioning: the "people not technology" frame is fully saturated at the enterprise/C-suite level, but the **individual-employee, empathetic, AI-native "walk you across the bridge"** angle — exactly NanoClaw/Shellano's positioning — is the clearest white space.
